regions.full_page: "Now Mrs. Wheeler, I have a little proposition for you to make yourself to the good God in your own honest way". "I'll do anything to please the good God", she interposed, "if He will only spare my poor, dear Husband"! "Vell this is the proposition or promise I want you to make, if you choose this rather than something else, whereby to please God. It is more a suggestion, therefore, that you promise or earnestly resolve in your own mind to look into the claimes of that "Mother Church" divinely planned and proclaimed infallible, and the claims of any other denomination or system of religion. Or I might say that you look into the con- nection between them". ..... Mr. Wheeler came home the next day - the day before yesterday and is here with his wife and neighbor To-day. A patch of about three inches square was like taped a- round and above his right temple. While I was noting the surprise, he remarked to the party who had given him his place: " ... its great to feel normal again, though I feel a little weak. Drs. in Ann Arbor, Peet and Wood, call it miraculous ... that a patient should talk intelligently inside of twenty-four hours after such an operation". Thanks be to God". I had not heard from them for over a year and a half, when Mrs. Wheeler came to lament the her husband was not very well of late. I asked her if she had kept her promise as I had sug- gested and if she had read the book I had lent her - "The Mysti- cal City of God". She humbly admitted that she had not. She had come without him, as she said, because she wanted to tell me about him first. I told her without hisitation: "The whole trouble is in your failure to keep your promise, or your proposition whatever it was". She promised to return next night with her husband and in the meantime to do something to show her good will. It was very stormy the next evening, so that she phoned their inability to come as promised but that they would come the following eve- ning. Following is the note I made under the original: Oct. 18th, 1944. Thank God they are both here To-day. He has started to read the said, won- derful life of the Blessed Virgin, the "Mystical City of God" and is quite enthused about it". Among other things in praise the wonderful work, the "Mystical City: which has been referred to as the autobiography of the Bl. Virgin herself, he remarked: "I find so much in it that I have often wondered about.
